sources.title: NVIDIA 800 VDC Architecture
sources.evidence_summary: 800 VDC is an emerging technical route for reducing conversion stages and supporting denser future AI racks. Higher AI rack power necessarily means copper interconnect captures more value across all architectures. All transformers, switchgear, UPS, PDU, and power-conversion suppliers benefit uniformly from the 800 VDC transition. New HVDC and 800 VDC architectures can shift, consolidate, or remove legacy conversion and distribution stages, so aggregate demand growth does not guarantee equal benefit for every incumbent equipment supplier.
sources.limitations: Company disclosures often combine AI data-center products with broader data-center, cooling, power, or cloud segments. Node-level revenue, gross margin, customer concentration, order visibility, and supplier allocation remain incomplete for several mappings.
sources.notes: Accepted for NVIDIA's declared 800 VDC technical route and its intended reduction in conversion stages, current, copper use, and cable bulk.
